title: Operator investigation syllabus and trace observatory
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight syllabus for ops investigators and engineers to run structured drills (and teach new hires) for inference incidents: latency regressions, KV cache cold tails, and multi-model fanout regressions. It bundles a small, repeatable investigation sequence, canonical metric definitions we use in drills, trace anchoring patterns, and a compact dashboard checklist for rapid hypothesis validation.

Audience:
- Oncall operators and SREs
- Serving/runtime engineers doing incident root-cause
- New observability hires (2–6 weeks ramp)

High-level goals:
1) Reduce median time-to-first-hypothesis by standardizing the first 10 checks.
2) Provide a reproducible trace anchoring pattern so traces tell the same story across incidents.
3) Keep a small, stable set of metrics (5–7) that cover latency, kvcache, and fanout cost.
4) Teach a simple experiment/rollback loop for rollout regressions.

Canonical metric set (short-form definitions used in drillbook):
- token_ttf_first_byte_ms: measured at the edge when the first response byte is sent to client (include streaming startup).
- model_infer_latency_p50_p95_ms: end-to-end infer call latency inside model pool (exclude queue time); p50 & p95 tracked.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: fraction of requests that read the KV prefix from memory vs fetch from model (window=5m tenant-weighted).
- kv_evict_rate_per_min: number of KV eviction events per minute per model-pool.
- batch_size_mean: average sequence batch size delivered to a model instance (helps detect forced singletons).
- multi_model_fanout_count: number of models touched per request on average (captures routing policy changes).
- tenant_tail_latency_fraction: fraction of tenants with 99th percentile > SLO threshold (tenant-aware triage).

Metric guardrails (how to use the numbers in practice):
- Use kv_cache_hit_ratio and kv_evict_rate together: if hit_ratio drops and evict_rate spikes, suspect eviction policy change or memory pressure.
- model_infer_latency_p95 drift without matching queue time increase -> likely kernel/compilation or model weight change.
- token_ttf_first_byte_ms up with batch_size_mean down -> batching/prefetch regressions or throttling.
- If multi_model_fanout_count increases after deploy, follow routing policy diffs and rollout tags.

Trace anchoring patterns (practical templates):
Anchor 1: client-edge -> routing -> model-pool -> kv-cache lookup -> kernel-infer -> response.
- Important span tags: request_id, tenant_id, model_version, pool_id, route_policy, kv_hit (true|false), batch_size.
- Use a fixed span ordering in trace UI so that kv-cache lookup spans appear before kernel-infer spans for readability.
- Sample rule: always capture full traces for 1% of requests, and 100% for requests that hit p99 latency or kv_hit=false and tenant in known customer list.

Anchor 2: rollout-path trace (for rollout debugging):
- Capture routing decision details (why a request fell back to variant B). Tag spans with rollout_flag and canary_bucket.
- If fallback occurred, include the upstream decision span with the prior call's model_version to show chaining.

Compact dashboard checklist (the minimal operator canvas):
Top row (fast sanity):
- token_ttf_first_byte_ms p50/p95 sparkline (1h/24h)
- model_infer_latency_p95 heatmap by model_version
- kv_cache_hit_ratio trend + per-tenant distribution (boxplot)
Middle row (drill):
- kv_evict_rate_per_min by pool_id
- batch_size_mean histogram by route_policy
- multi_model_fanout_count timeseries and per-tenant breakdown
Bottom row (cost & tenants):
- tenant_tail_latency_fraction list table (tenants sorted by p99 delta)
- recent traces quicklinks for p99 anomalies (auto-populated)

Investigation-first sequence (10-minute starter run):
1) Confirm whether increase is in token_ttf_first_byte_ms or model_infer_latency_p95 (dash top row).
2) If token_ttf_first_byte_ms: check edge/router logs for throttling, rate-limits, or CDN issues.
3) If model_infer_latency_p95: check model_pool queue_time metric. If queue_time unchanged, go to traces.
4) Open 3 representative traces from p95 group across different tenants and compare kv_hit tag and batch_size.
5) If kv_hit=false on p95 traces, check kv_evict_rate and pool memory stats; escalate to infra if memory pressure.
6) If batch_size_mean dropped for affected routes, review batching autoscaling and recent config PRs.
7) If multi_model_fanout_count increased: inspect routing-policy diff and rollout tags.
8) Always run tenant_tail_latency_fraction to prioritize customer-impact.
9) Draft timeline and rollback window; if suspected config/rollout, mark change in incident timeline and page the release owner.
10) If root cause unclear after traces, promote to deep-dive and add hypothesis cards for model compile, kernel path changes, or hardware jitter.

Teaching labs (for new operators):
- Lab 1: KV cold-tail simulation: synthetic traffic with a long-prefill gap, watch kv_cache_hit_ratio drop and recover. Exercise: adjust eviction TTL and observe metrics.
- Lab 2: Batch starvation: Run many single-token requests and watch batch_size_mean and model_infer_latency.
- Lab 3: Rollout safety: Create A/B routing change in staging and verify traces show rollout_flag and canary_bucket. Practice rollback and trace comparison.

Experiment protocol (how to test hypotheses safely in prod):
- Start in synthetic canary lanes (1–2% tenants) for 30m.
- Measure the canonical metric set and compare to baseline using the dashboard's experiment mode.
- Keep a written hypothesis and success criteria in the incident doc (linked_artifacts).
- If experiment passes, scale to 10% for another 30m. If fails at any stage, rollback immediately and attach traces to the rollout PR.

Mini runbook notes (quick commands & queries):
- SQL-ish metric query: SELECT tenant_id, percentile(latency, 95) FROM model_infer WHERE time > now()-1h GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY percentile DESC LIMIT 20;
- Trace search pattern: tags:kv_hit=false OR tags:batch_size<2 AND model_pool:gpu-v2; filter p95 latency > 500ms.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add a lightweight synthesized probe that approximates kv_cache_hit_ratio per-tenant (Q1 2026).
- Consolidate span tag naming across runtime and router (some services still use "kv_hit_flag"). TODO: rename or alias. (See ENG-4903).
- Investigate automatic trace-anchoring heuristics to attach the most-representative trace to dashboard anomalies.

Notes to self / shorthand (rough):
- Keep dashboards lean: 7 panels max in operator kit.
- Teach: trace anchors > single span histogram. Getting the right trace is half the battle.
- When in doubt, escalate to model-runtime oncall and include at least 3 representative traces in the page.

Pointers & links:
- Confluence: trace-observatory (see linked_artifacts)
- GitHub: telemetry PRs that modify span-tags (linked)
- Jira: ENG-4821 (kv eviction policy incident template)

Appendix: short glossary for new hires:
- kv warmth: shorthand for how often prefixes are served from memory vs computed; not a direct metric but inferred from hit ratio + time-since-last-prefix.
- anchor trace: a representative full-trace selected to illustrate the dominant latency path for that incident.
- rollout_flag: attribute on routing spans that carries canary metadata.

End of doc.

(If you pull this into the ops runbook, please add your name and date in the header and record one successful drill run as an example.)
